title: The United Nations & post-war order
examples: What was the main goal of the United Nations?
How did the Bretton Woods system work for money?
What are the main parts of the UN?

explain.say: The United Nations was formed after the Second World War. It aimed to keep peace globally. It created a new system for international cooperation.

draw.text: UN formed after WWII for peace.

explain.say: The UN has several main bodies. The General Assembly is where all member states meet. They discuss global issues together.
Another key body is the Security Council. It has the power to make decisions on peace threats. Some major powers have veto power there.
The Bretton Woods system created global financial rules. It established the International Monetary Fund. This helped stabilize world currencies.
The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development was also part of this. It provided loans for rebuilding nations. This was vital after the war.
In everyday life, the UN helps coordinate disaster relief efforts. For example, after an earthquake, they organize aid from many countries. This shows global teamwork.

faq.q: How effective was the UN really?
faq.a: The UN has succeeded in preventing many large-scale wars. However, its effectiveness is often limited by the disagreements between its major member states.
asks: Does the UN always solve problems?
Are there limits to UN power?

faq.q: What is the difference between the General Assembly and the Security Council?
faq.a: The General Assembly is a place for discussion by all members. The Security Council has specific powers to enforce peace decisions.
asks: Which UN body is more powerful?
What is the role of the Security Council?

faq.q: What was the main purpose of Bretton Woods?
faq.a: Its main purpose was to create a stable international monetary system. This stopped the economic instability seen before the war.
asks: Why did they need Bretton Woods?
What economic problem did it solve?

faq.q: Does the UN control all countries?
faq.a: No, the UN relies on the cooperation of its member states. It can recommend actions but cannot force every country to comply.
asks: Can the UN make laws for everyone?

faq.q: What is 'veto power' in the Security Council?
faq.a: Veto power allows one of the five permanent members to block any resolution. This can cause major disagreements and stop action.
asks: What is the impact of a veto?

facts: The UN was established in 1945 following the devastation of World War Two.
The General Assembly allows all member states to participate in discussions.
Bretton Woods established a system to stabilize international currency exchange rates.
The Security Council can pass resolutions regarding international peace and security.

quiz.say: The UN's main goal after 1945 was to:
quiz.why: The formation of the UN was a direct response to the devastation of two world wars.

wrong.0: Its focus is on cooperation, not direct border control.
wrong.2: This was more related to the economic goals of Bretton Woods.
wrong.3: The UN respects the sovereignty of its member nations.

quiz.say: Which body has the power to make binding decisions on peace threats?
quiz.why: The Security Council is specifically tasked with maintaining international peace and security.

wrong.0: The General Assembly discusses issues but cannot enforce decisions.
wrong.1: This body deals with finance, not security threats.
wrong.2: This institution focuses primarily on development loans.

quiz.say: The Bretton Woods system primarily aimed to fix:
quiz.why: The system was designed to prevent the currency instability that led to trade wars.

wrong.0: Tariffs are managed by trade agreements, not the currency system itself.
wrong.1: The system was purely economic in nature.
wrong.2: Military alliances are political structures, not financial ones.
